rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge applies to the Qur’an and portions of it, demonstrating the truth of Muhammad’s prophethood.
rows.anchor: فلذلك صح التحدي بسورة مرة، وبعشر سور مرة، وبكل القرآن مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is revealed as it stands, not composed in ʿUthmān’s time as some claimed; this validates the challenges by one surah, ten, or all of the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن هذه السورة كما هي منزلة لا كما زعم بعضهم أنه نظم أيام عثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is God’s speech and not human speech.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن القرآن كلام الله تعالى، وليس من كلام البشر

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The general reading has waqūduhā with fatḥa on the wāw.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: وقودها بفتح الواو

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid are reported to read the wāw with ḍamma, which the author rejects as incorrect.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ومجاهد بضم الواو، وليس بصحيح

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmayr is reported to read waqīduhā, but the author rejects it because Qur’anic reading must be widely transmitted.
rows.anchor: وعن عبيد بن عمير: وقيدها، ولا يجوز القراءة بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, waqūd means fuel or firewood; with ḍamma, it means kindling.
rows.anchor: والوقود بالفتح الحطب، وبالضم الإيقاد

rows.speaker: ابن الخليل
rows.claim: Fiʿl, iḥdāth, and ījād are near-synonyms; the two vocalizations of fiʿl distinguish verbal noun from noun, as Ibn al-Khalīl explains.
rows.anchor: فالمفتوح المصدر، والمكسور الاسم، هكذا ذكره ابن الخليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An act implies its agent is capable; awaiting or ordering acts implies knowledge, and mediation implies that the agent exists and is living.
rows.anchor: الفعل بنفسه يدل على كون فاعله قادرا، وبانتظار أو بانتظام الفعل على كونه عالما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijāra is the singular of ḥajar, an irregular formation; the regular plural would be aḥjār.
rows.anchor: والحجارة واحدها حجر، وليس بقياس، فالقياس أحجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿdād means preparing something for someone, as in the command to prepare against them.
rows.anchor: والإعداد: مصدر أعد له كذا، أي هيأ، ومنه: (وأعدوا لهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-lan tafʿalū is a parenthetical interruption, as parentheticals can separate a condition from its consequence.
rows.anchor: كما يتصل الاعتراض بين المبتدأ والخبر، وبين الشرط والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical view gives the clause no syntactic position because no governing element acts on it.
rows.anchor: فقيل: لا موضع لها من الإعراب؛ إذ لم يعمل فيها عامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author illustrates parenthetical clauses with 3:30, where innā lā nuḍīʿu interrupts the sentence and the predicate follows afterward.
rows.anchor: فقوله: (إنا لا نضيع) اعتراض، والخبر: أولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse requires honoring covenants and condemns breaking them, including God’s commands, vows, oaths, and contracts.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على وجوب الوفاء بالعهد وقبح نقضه، فيدخل فيه أوامر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It requires maintaining ties with relatives and believers and condemns severing those ties.
rows.anchor: وتدل على وجوب صلة الرحم وصلة المؤمن وقبح قطعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever disobeys God deserves the Fire, and whoever enters it has suffered manifest loss.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن من عصى الله فقد استوجب النار، ومن دخلها فقد خسر خسرانا مبينا ..

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the relevant yāʾ and tāʾ forms with fatḥa as active verbs throughout the Qur’an; other readers use passive forms, with exceptions.
rows.anchor: قرأ يعقوب في الياء والتاء بفتحها على أن الفعل لهم في جميع القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is the opposite of life, and the two alternate in living beings.
rows.anchor: الموت ضد الحياة، وهما يتعاقبان على الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life is an accident by which humans and other animals live, and only God can bring it about.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أن الحياة عرض يحيا به الإنسان وسائر الحيوانات، ولا يقدر عليه إلا الله

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: Most hold that death is an accident opposed to life, citing God’s creation of death and life.
rows.anchor: فالأكثر على أنه عرض يضاد الحياة؛ ولذلك قال: (خلق الموت والحياة)

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم
rows.claim: Abū Hāshim is reported to hold that death is not a positive entity or accident.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ليس بمعنى، عن أبي هاشم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To return to something means to go back to it.
rows.anchor: والرجوع في الشيء: هو العود إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayfa asks about a state and ranges over all states, just as kam ranges over numbers, mā over kinds, ayna over places, and man over rational beings.
rows.anchor: و(كيف) ينتظم جميع الأحوال، كما أن (كم) ينتظم جميع الأعداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna governs a nominative subject and accusative predicate; it has complete, incomplete, extra, and implicit-subject uses.
rows.anchor: وعمله أن يرفع الاسم وينصب الخبر، تقول: كان زيد قائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna is conjugated like a verb but is not truly a verb: it indicates time and enters a nominal subject-predicate construction.
rows.anchor: فليس بفعل على الحقيقة وإنما يدل على الزمان، ويدخل على الابتداء والخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna has complete, incomplete, extra, and implicit-subject uses.
rows.anchor: و (كان) على أربعة أوجه: تامة، وناقصة، وزائدة، ومضمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its extra use, kāna adds emphasis while its entry can be removed without changing the sentence’s basic meaning.
rows.anchor: والزائدة: ما يكون دخولها كخروجها إلا بمقدار ما توجبه من التوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates extra kāna with 19:29, explaining the statement as asking how they could speak to a child in the cradle.
rows.anchor: أي كيف نكلم من في المهد صبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second life refers to the grave and its punishment; reading it as life in Paradise would make the following return to God incoherent.
rows.anchor: على الحياة في الجنة لم يستقم قوله: ثم إليه ترجعون؛ لأن تلك الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that people return to God establishes resurrection.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله ثم إليه ترجعون على إثبات المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God bestowed blessings on unbelievers, contrary to the Mujbira claim that He grants them no favor.
rows.anchor: وتدل الآية على أنه تعالى أنعم على الكفار؛ لذلك عد عليهم ما عد بخلاف قول المجبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly benefits still count as favors even if the unbeliever is destined for the Fire; they are like a poisoned dish and are diminished by grave wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ولا يحمل على نعم الدنيا؛ لأنه إذا كان خلقه للنار لم يعتد بنعم الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s power to give life a second time follows from His power to give it the first time.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه قادر على الإحياء الثاني من حيث قدر على الإحياء الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Greater benefaction makes disobedience to the benefactor more serious; hence the rebuke, How can you disbelieve?
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن عظم النعمة يوجب عظم معصية المنعم، لذلك قال: كيف تكفرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamʿ and ḍamm are near-synonyms; jamʿ is opposed to dispersal, and Friday and the place Jamʿ are named for gathering.
rows.anchor: الجمع والضم نظائر، ونقيض الجمع الفرق، ويقال: جمعه جمعا، وفرقه فرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gathering and separation are accidents in the genus of colors and indicate that bodies are originated.
rows.anchor: والاجتماع والافتراق عرضان من جنس الألوان، يدلان على حدث الجسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, istawā can mean became straight, turned toward, gained control, or rose and ascended; this passage does not select one sense.
rows.anchor: والاستواء في اللغة ينصرف على أربعة أوجه: استوى: استقام، وهو الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taswiya means straightening or adjusting; its essential sense is to make a thing even.
rows.anchor: والتسوية: التقويم، وحقيقتها جعل الشيء على الاستواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabʿ and sabʿa have feminine and masculine patterns respectively, though gender marking can depart from the regular pattern.
rows.anchor: والسبع للمؤنث، والسبعة للمذكر، وقد جاء التأنيث والتذكير على خلاف الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlīm means knowing like ʿālim, but carries a stronger intensive force.
rows.anchor: وعليم: فعيل من علم، ومعناه عالم، غير أن في عليم مبالغة ليست في عالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some hold all such things to be prohibited, while others suspend judgment; the author says the verse confirms his own position.
rows.anchor: قوم: جميع ذلك على الحظر، وقال بعضهم: على التوقف، والآية تدل على صحة ما قلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge of everything refutes Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam’s claim that God knows created things through newly originated knowledge.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه تعالى عالم بكل شيء، فيبطل قول هشام بن الحكم

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm says that creating seven heavens from smoke demonstrates God’s power to resurrect the dead.
rows.anchor: قال الأصم: وتدل على البعث؛ لأن من قدر على خلق سبع سماوات من دخان

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The general reading is khalīfa with fāʾ.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة (خليفة) بالفاء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some are reported to read khalīqa with qāf, meaning a created being; although meaningful, the author rejects it for lacking widely transmitted reading.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم: (خليقة) بالقاف يعني خلقا، وهذا وإن كان له معنى صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malak derives from the language of sending a message: alīkni means send me, and maʾlaka or alūk means message; the original hamza was dropped for ease.
rows.anchor: الملك: أصله من الرسالة، يقال: ألكني إليه، أي أرسلني، والمألكة الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malak has the pattern mafʿal after deletion of its hamza and became the established name for a class of God’s nonhuman messengers.
rows.anchor: فصار ملك، وهو الرسول، ووزنه مفعل؛ لأن أصله ملأك حذفت الهمزة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poet preserves the original hamza in malāʾak; the author says this form is otherwise used only under poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: فلست لإنسي ولكن لملأك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jaʿl changes something from its prior state without bringing it into existence, unlike fiʿl and iḥdāth.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الجعل يتعلق بالشيء لا على سبيل الإيجاد، بخلاف الفعل، والإحداث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalīfa and imām overlap in use, but khalīfa succeeds another while imām leads a group and is to be obeyed.
rows.anchor: والخليفة والإمام واحد في الاستعمال، وبينهما فرق، والخليفة مأخوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaf with fatḥa on the lām denotes righteous successors, while sukūn denotes bad successors, as illustrated in 7:169.
rows.anchor: والخلف بنصب اللام من الصالحين، وبسكون اللام من الطالحين؛ قال تعالى: (فخلف من بعدهم خلف)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh normally refers to the past and idhā to the future, though either can stand in place of the other.
rows.anchor: ويقال: (إذ) لما مضى، و(إذا) لما يستقبل، فيوضع أحدهما موضع الآخر

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says idh with a future verb takes past-time meaning, while idhā with a past verb takes future-time meaning; he cites 8:30, 79:34, and 110:1.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: إذا جاء (إذ) مع المستقبل كان معناه على الماضي كقوله تعالى: (وإذ يمكر)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The governing verb for idh is omitted, with the primary estimate wa-udhkur idh, remember when.
rows.anchor: قلنا: محذوف، تقديره: واذكر إذ قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another estimate ties this to the beginning of creation: God began creating people when He said this.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما ذكر خلق السماوات دل على ابتداء الخلق، فكأنه قال: وابتدأ خلقكم إذ قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further estimate is that God knew their states when He spoke to the angels.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وهو عليم بأحوالكم إذ قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier how-can-you-disbelieve clause itself implies an omitted remember, supporting the estimate remember when God spoke.
rows.anchor: وفي الوجه الأول في الكلام دليل على المحذوف؛ لأن قوله: (كيف تكفرون)

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet’s line supports ellipsis: after a conditional أينما, the understood verb ذهب is omitted.
rows.anchor: قال الشا عر: فإن المنية من يخشها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Zajjāj parse the hamza as affirmative, citing Jarīr’s ألستم as a parallel.
rows.anchor: ألف إيجاب عن أبي عبيدة والزجاج، كقول جرير: ألستم خير من ركب المطايا

rows.speaker: غيرهما
rows.claim: Other grammarians take the hamza as interrogative: the angels ask whether they are placed alongside a corrupter despite their glorification.
rows.anchor: وقال غيرهما: هو ألف استفهام كأنهم قالوا: أتجعل فيها من يفسد وهذه حالنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the interrogative: it asks about the angels’ state relative to the appointment, not whether God will appoint a successor.
rows.anchor: والصواب هو الثاني، وإنما غلط من زعم أنها ألف إيجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative does not imply doubt that God will appoint a successor; it asks whether the angels’ state and the appointment are equally sound.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يصح؛ لأن الاستفهام لا يوجب الشك في أنه سيجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis treats the lām as extra and reads the phrase as nuqaddisuka, we sanctify You.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله: ونقدس لك قيل: صلة، تقديره: نقدسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis treats the lām as expressing purpose: we sanctify for Your sake and pleasure.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لام الإضافة، أي نقدس لأجلك ورضاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account connects the verse to preceding favors: human creation and life, earthly things, heaven, then Adam and blessings to his descendants.
rows.anchor: اتصاله بما قبله أنه عد النعم والحجج، فبدأ بذكر خلق الإنسان وحياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the passage gathers evidence for divine unity from earth and heaven, then follows with the beginning of creation and Adam.
rows.anchor: وقيل: احتج عليهم بالتوحيد فجمع الأدلة في الأرض والسماوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed question is how God could create beings He knows will disbelieve, when all His acts are good and He cannot do wrong.
rows.anchor: الخامس: أشكل عليهم خلق من يعلم أنه يكفر ممن جميع أفعاله حسنة، ولا يجوز عليه القبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed question is why God would create corrupters and then defer their punishment.
rows.anchor: السادس: أشكل عليهم خلق المفسدين مع الإمهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further proposal is that the angels wondered whether God’s successor could be corrupt and sinful.
rows.anchor: السابع: أشكل عليهم أن خليفة الله هل يجوز أن يكون مفسدا فاسقا أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the angels were not puzzled but asked, magnifying God, that He not create anyone who would disobey; another reads the words as astonishment at a creature disobeying its creator.
rows.anchor: أنه لم يشكل عليهم شيء ولكن سؤالهم على وجه للمبالغة في إعظامه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels asked with God’s permission, which He granted because He knew asking benefited them.
rows.anchor: بل بإذن لهم في السؤال لما علم من مصلحتهم في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that the angels declare God transcendent above bodily attributes and purify Him of reprehensible acts.
rows.anchor: قيل: ننزهك عن صفات الأجسام، ونقدسك عن قبائح الأفعال

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets the angels’ tasbīḥ as the familiar act of glorification.
rows.anchor: المراد التسبيح المعروف، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the angels’ tasbīḥ as prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الصلاة، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says they glorify God by attributing blessings to Him and praising Him for them.
rows.anchor: ننزهك بإضافة النعم إليك، ونحمدك على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says glorification benefits the angels, while their ability to perform it comes from God’s enabling.
rows.anchor: لأن نفع التسبيح عائد إلينا، وهو بتوفيقك

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim takes the angels’ sanctification as purifying themselves from sins for God’s sake and pleasure.
rows.anchor: نطهر أنفسنا عن المعاصي ابتغاء مرضاتك، دليله نقدس لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account treats the lām as extra and the sanctification as directed to God Himself.
rows.anchor: اللام صلة، والتقديس يرجع إلى الله تعالى، وتقديره: نقدسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the angels asked God to make them the earthly inhabitants because earthly duties would be lighter.
rows.anchor: قيل: نعم؛ لأن تكليف أهل الأرض أخف

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says they asked to be placed on earth because it would benefit them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سألوا ذلك بأن كان لهم فيه صلاح، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One rejects that they asked to replace people because this implies a divine will without evidence; another rearranges the phrase to mean they glorify by God’s guidance and then praise Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا؛ لأنه حكم بإرادتهم، وذلك لا يصح من غير دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God knows prophets, scholars, and saints will arise among Adam’s descendants and knows their great work in religion and worldly affairs.
rows.anchor: قيل: يعلم أن في ذريته أنبياء وعلماء وأولياء، وقيل: أعلم منهم من عظيم حالهم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says God knows the interests involved and which location is best for angels and people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أعلم من المصالح، وأي موضع أصلح لهم ولكم ما لا تعلمون، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed meaning is God’s knowledge of Iblīs’s concealed disobedience, but the author rejects it because Iblīs has not yet been mentioned.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أعلم من إضمار إبليس المعصية ما لا تعلمون، وليس بالوجه؛ لأنه لم يجر له ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author questions how declaring God transcendent can fit the Jabriyya view that all injustice, obscenity, and corruption are created and willed by God.
rows.anchor: كيف يصح التنزيه. وتدل على أن خلق من يعلم أنه يكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating people whom God knows will disbelieve can still be wise and right.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن خلق من يعلم أنه يكفر يكون حكمة وصوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s answer implies He does not do evil; it is meaningful as an appeal to knowledge of governance and interests, leading Him to do what is best.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: (أعلم ما لا تعلمون) على أنه لا يفعل القبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s address to the angels establishes that they are accountable beings.
rows.anchor: وتدل على إثبات المكلف فإنه تعالى خاطبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels are a distinct kind of living creature, with wings, no eating, drinking, or sexual relations; their subtlety makes them invisible unless God strengthens our vision or gives them density.
rows.anchor: والملك حيوان معروف متميز عن سائر الخلق بالصورة، وبأنهم لا يأكلون ولا يشربون ولا ينكحون

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author’s school holds angels to be accountable and free agents, while another group says they are compelled.
rows.anchor: فقال أصحابنا: هم مكلفون ومختارون، وقال جماعة: مجبورون

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author’s school holds angels sinless, citing 66:6; another view says they are not sinless.
rows.anchor: فقال أصحابنا: هم معصومون لقول الله تعالى: (لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: One group says believers are superior to angels; another says angels surpass believers but prophets surpass angels.
rows.anchor: فقيل: المؤمنون أفضل منهم، وهو قول جماعة، وقيل: هم أفضل من المؤمنين، والأنبياء أفضل منهم

rows.speaker: جماعة من الإمامية
rows.claim: Some Imāmīs hold prophets and Imams superior to angels; other views single out the Prophet or suspend judgment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأنبياء والأئمة أفضل منهم وهو قول جماعة من الإمامية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other positions say only the Prophet is superior to angels, or that the ranking is unknown and judgment should be suspended.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نبينا أفضل منهم فقط، وقيل: لا يعلم ذلك، ويتوقف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s position is that angels are superior to all prophets, citing Qur’anic statements about not being an angel, becoming two angels, and Christ and the nearest angels serving God.
rows.anchor: وعندنا: الملائكة أفضل من جميع الأنبياء؛ ولذلك قال تعالى: (ولا أقول لكم إني ملك)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command cannot be a kindness coinciding with what it facilitates: death removes life, and a kindness must precede the act it facilitates.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز كونه لطفا فيما يقارنه لوجهين: أحدهما: أن بوقوعه تنتفي الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is not obligated to bear hardship as a kindness to another; likewise, warding off another’s harm is not a basis of obligation.
rows.anchor: يكلف دفع الضرر عن غيره؛ لأن ذلك ليس بوجه وجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked whether this reasoning permits God to command someone to cut a hand or foot as a kindness, the author says it does.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل: على معنى هذا وجب أن يجوز أن يأمر بقطع يده أو رجله لطفا له؟ قلنا: يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calf worship is attributed to the people, and they were commanded to repent and punished; this establishes human agency.
rows.anchor: وتدل الآية على أن للعبد فعلا؛ لأنه أضاف عبادة العجل إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance may require something beyond remorse, here the commanded killing.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن التوبة قد يشترط فيه سوى الندم ما لا تصح التوبة إلا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is unjust when they disobey God and violate His command.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن العبد يكون ظالما متى عصى الله وخالف أمره

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The general reading has jahra with a quiescent hāʾ.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة جهرة بسكون الهاء، وعن ابن عباس بفتحها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to read jahra with fatḥa on the hāʾ; both are language variants.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس بفتحها، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The general reading is al-ṣāʿiqa with an alif.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة الصاعقة بالألف، وعن عمر وعثمان وعلي

rows.speaker: عمر وعثمان وعلي
rows.claim: ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, and ʿAlī are reported to read al-ṣaʿqa without the alif; both forms are language variants.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر وعثمان وعلي رضي الله عنهم: الصعقة بغير ألف، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īmān means assent or belief, as in the brothers’ statement in 12:17.
rows.anchor: الإيمان: التصديق، ومنه: (وما أنت بمؤمن لنا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruʾya means perception by sight and is also used figuratively for knowledge of the heart; mirʾāt is named for seeing through it.
rows.anchor: والرؤية: الإدراك بالبصر، ثم يستعمل بمعنى العلم، ومنه رأى بقلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahr means openly and publicly, the opposite of secrecy; its basic sense is something appearing to direct inspection.
rows.anchor: والجهر والعلانية بمعنى يقال: جهر فلان بكلامه، وجهر بقراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṣāʿiqa originally is fire falling from the sky and burning what it strikes, then by extension can mean any punishment.
rows.anchor: والصاعقة: أصلها نار تنزل من السماء تحرق ما تأتي عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naẓar is turning the eye toward something visible in search of sight with a sound faculty, and can extend to thought.
rows.anchor: والنظر: تقليب الحدقة نحو المرئي التماسا لرؤيته مع سلامة الحاسة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The verb yarā is on the yafʿalu pattern because its original form is yarʾā; a poet preserves the original form.
rows.anchor: لأن أصله يرأى، قال الشاعر، وجاء به على الأصل: أري عيني ما لم ترأياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahratan is parsed as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: وجهرة: نصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address means remember when you said this; it refers to the ancestors of the Jews addressed in Muhammad’s time, whom they followed.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى خصلة من خصال أسلافهم فقال تعالى: وإذ قلتم أي اذكروا إذ قلتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that they would not believe Moses’ description of God’s attributes until they saw God directly.
rows.anchor: لا نصدقك فيما تصف الله به من الصفات حتى نراه جهرة

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm says they meant they would not believe Moses was a prophet until they saw God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا نصدقك في نبوتك، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes jahra describe the seeing, while another makes it describe their public statement.
rows.anchor: فعلى الأول الجهرة من صفة الرؤية، وعلى الثاني من صفة المقالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thunderbolt can mean death, as in 39:68.
rows.anchor: الصاعقة تستعمل على ثلاثة أوجه: الموت كقوله تعالى: (فصعق من في السماوات)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thunderbolt can mean punishment, as in the warning about a punishment like that of ʿĀd and Thamūd.
rows.anchor: الثاني: العذاب، كقوله: (أنذرتكم صاعقة مثل صاعقة عاد وثمود)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can also mean fire sent down from the sky, as in the statement that God sends thunderbolts.
rows.anchor: والثالث: نار تسقط من السماء، كقوله: (ويرسل الصواعق)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people were looking at or witnessing the event.
rows.anchor: وأنتم تنظرون يعني تعاينونه وترونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are blamed for their ancestors’ demand because they approved the action and followed their predecessors in opposing the one they had to follow.
rows.anchor: ويقال: لم قرعوا بسؤال أسلافهم الرؤية؟ قلنا: لأنهم رضوا بفعلهم وسلكوا طريقتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says this condemns the Jews and consoles the Prophet, since his opponents repeat their ancestors’ opposition to Moses and impossible demands.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فيه ذم لهم وتسلية للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في أنهم بمخالفتهم إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collective address is to Jews in Muhammad’s time, while the demand came from some ancestors; God summarizes the ancestors’ crimes.
rows.anchor: هذا خطاب لليهود الذين كانوا في زمن نبينا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وكان هذا القول وجد من بعض أسلافهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vision can be inward or in a dream; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses jahra as publicly and Qatāda as seeing with the eyes.
rows.anchor: قد تكون كرؤية القلب، والرؤية في النوم، وقيل: علانية، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking for vision was unbelief by consensus because it rejected the messenger; permitting vision with anthropomorphic likeness is also unbelief.
rows.anchor: هذا السؤال كفر بالإجماع؛ لأنه رد على الرسول، فأما إجازة الرؤية على جهة التشبيه فكفر

rows.speaker: أبو علي وأبو هاشم
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī and Abū Hāshim say permitting vision without anthropomorphic likeness is not unbelief.
rows.anchor: وإجازتها من غير تشبيه قيل: ليس بكفر، عن أبي علي وأبي هاشم

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم
rows.claim: Abū al-Qāsim says permitting vision without anthropomorphic likeness is still unbelief.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كفر، عن أبي القاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author ties the people’s punishment to their demand to see God and concludes that vision of God is impossible.
rows.anchor: وأنزل العقوبة بهم. وتدل على أن الرؤية لا تجوز عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God condemned the bare request for vision, without regard to any added qualification of how it would occur.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى أنكر عليهم مجرد سؤال الرؤية، ولم يعتبر الزيادة التي أوردها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for the severity is that anything perceived by sight must have a quality such as body or color, so allowing vision entails likeness; another says they explicitly coupled vision with likeness by saying jahra.
rows.anchor: فجواز الرؤية يقتضي التشبيه، وقيل: لأنهم قرنوا الرؤية بالتشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severe punishment cut off the source of this demand for them and others.
rows.anchor: لما عظم سؤالهم عاقبهم حتى يحسم مادة السؤال منهم ومن غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thunderbolt descended but did not compel them to know; otherwise restoring them and holding them accountable would be improper.
rows.anchor: وتدل الآية على أن الصاعقة نزلت، ولم يضطروا إلى المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After proof has been established, a community’s statement to its messenger that it will not believe is unbelief.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن قول الأمة للرسول بعد إقامة الحجة: (لن نؤمن لك) كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’ divinely enabled miracles show that natural processes do not constrain God, refuting the claim that offspring necessarily require semen and both a male and female.
rows.anchor: وأبرئ الأكمه والأبرص وأحي الموتى بإذن الله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وعاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, and Yaʿqūb read yuʿallimuhu with yāʾ; the other readers use nūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وعاصم ويعقوب يعلمه بالياء والباقون بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ reading can coordinate with yakhluqu as a report voiced by the angel, or with yubashshiruka, as al-Mubarrad proposes.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عطفا على يبشرك عن المبرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn reading can coordinate with nuḥīhi ilayka and begin God’s own speech; the author prefers it as more majestic.
rows.anchor: وأما النون فعطف على نوحيه إليك ويكون كلام الله تعالى ابتداء، أو هو أولى؛ لأنه أفخم

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads innī with kasra; the other readers use fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع إني أخلق بكسر الألف من (إن) والباقون بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥa reading attaches to messengerhood or supplies an omitted preposition, bi-annī or li-annī; kasra begins an independent clause.
rows.anchor: فمن فتح فلوقوع الرسالة عليه، وقيل: بنزع حرف الصفة أي بأني أو لأني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra reading treats the statement as a fresh independent sentence.
rows.anchor: ومن كسر فعلى الاستئناف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads the word with a doubled yāʾ; other readers use hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر كهية بتشديد الياء والآخرون بالهمز

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, and Yaʿqūb read ṭāʾiran in the singular; the rest read ṭayran collectively, likewise in 5:110.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع ويعقوب فيكون طائرا بالألف على الواحد

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The general reading has the second-person tāʾ in taddakhirūn.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة: وما تدخرون بالتاء، وعن مجاهد بالياء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid is reported to read the verb with yāʾ rather than tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭīn means clay; ṭayyanat al-kitāb means clay was placed on the document.
rows.anchor: الطين معروف، يقال: طينت الكتاب جعلت عليه طينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayʾa is the visible state or appearance; the verb hāʾa describes a fine appearance.
rows.anchor: والهيئة: الحال الظاهرة هاء فلان يهاء هيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafkh is air that comes out of the mouth.
rows.anchor: والنفخ: ريح يخرج من الفم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭayr is a collective plural whose singular is ṭāʾir, like zūr from zāʾir and safar from sāfir.
rows.anchor: والطير جمع، واحده: طائر نحو: زائر وزور، وسافر وسفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barʾ means healing, and akmah means blind.
rows.anchor: والبرء: الشفاء. والأكمه في اللغة الأعمى يقال: كمه يكمه كمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baras is the familiar disease, which Arabs regarded as ill-omened and which has no cure once firmly established.
rows.anchor: والبرص: الداء المعروف، وكان يتطير منه العرب، وإذا استحكم فلا برء له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iddikhar derives from d-kh-r and means hiding something for a future need; its morphology changes the tāʾ and assimilates the adjacent dhāl into dāl.
rows.anchor: والادخار: افتعال من الدخر، دخرت أدخر دخرا، وادخرت ادخارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes yuʿallimuhu accusative, coordinated with wajīhan: honored and a teacher.
rows.anchor: قيل: نصب بالعطف على وجيها تقديره: وجيها ومعلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse gives it no syntactic position because it coordinates with a sentence that has none, namely God creates what He wills.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا موضع له؛ لأنه عطف على جملة لا موضع لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parse coordinates it with nuḥīhi ilayka, but the author rejects this because it removes the clause from the glad tidings to Mary.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو معطوف على نوحيه إليك وليس بصحيح؛ لأنه يخرجه من معنى البشارة لمريم
